summary: Technical sync to align reference architecture and marketplace listing requirements. Covered VPC/on-prem deployment options, KMS and audit log expectations, helm/manifest delivery, and benchmark targets. Agreed next steps to deliver draft docs and schedule POC benchmark.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-03-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood) / Lena Park, Rajat Singh, Sofia Morales (AuroraCloud)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro from our side, I'm Maya AE, Diego is our systems eng, and we wanna make sure the reference architecture aligns with AuroraCloud marketplace requirements.
[00:18] Lena Park: Thanks Maya, I'm lena, product manager on the marketplace team, we own the listing process and the reference arch reqs, happy to go through constraints.
[00:35] Diego Alvarez: Hi all, Diego SE, i can take the deep infra bits — we've done a few market place listings, usually the tricky bits are VPC connectivity and KMS integrations.
[00:50] Rajat Singh: quick callout from infra, we need to confirm network egress policies, VPC peering, and if redwood private will support our IR policy.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Right, so overview: Redwood supports hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace reference arch we usually recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput but Private if you need VPC isolation and customer-managed networking.
[01:35] Sofia Morales: Can you clarify differences between Dedicated vs Private from an operational perspective? e.g., who manages KMS keys, where logs land?
[01:50] Diego Alvarez: Sure — Dedicated is still hosted by Redwood but isolated capacity, encryption at rest is by default with Redwood-managed KMS; for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM via standard CMEK patterns, and audit logs can ship to your central logging (we provide rbac + log forwarding).
[02:20] Lena Park: For marketplace listing we require a reference arch that shows: network flow, certificate handling, KMS, SSO options, and upgrade / rollback plan. Also need a short runbook for onboarding.
[02:40] Rajat Singh: Also need details on how model updates are handled; are you providing model artifacts in the chart, or pulling from a Redwood registry?
[02:55] Diego Alvarez: Good Q — for Private we have two options: we can provide a pre-baked model bundle (OCI style) or you can pull from Redwood's secured model registry during install. Both supported; for regulated customers we recommend OCI bundle with attestation.
[03:20] Maya Chen: Noted. On the marketplace side we should show both flows and call out the default recommended option (OCI bundle for air-gapped).
[03:38] [00:03:40] Lena Park: Timing wise, what's a typical POC timeline for private deployment? we need to map to our marketplace certification window.
[03:50] Diego Alvarez: For a small POC we usually do a 2-3 day ramp: day 1 infra + install (helm), day 2 benchmarks/load tests + tuning, day 3 follow-ups and any bugfixes. If you want a more formal performance test we can schedule a 2-3 hour benchmark window where we run our script against your VPC.
[04:12] Sofia Morales: ok that's reasonable. Do you have a helm chart and example values we can use?
[04:20] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have a published helm chart; I'll share the repo link and an example values.yaml (and a k8s manifest set) after call.
[04:35] Rajat Singh: On security — SOC2 scope, audit logs, SSO: does Redwood support SAML/SSO integrations and role-based access control? also, what about encryption of KV cache?
[04:55] Maya Chen: Yes to SAML/SSO and RBAC; we support SAML and OIDC flows and can map groups to roles. For KV cache encryption that's handled in the runtime — we encrypt KV stores at rest and in motion, and for private deployments you can add an HSM-backed KMS.
[05:20] Lena Park: For marketplace docs we need the data flow diagram to show how requests traverse from AuroraCloud customers to Redwood runtime and where data is stored/retained. Any chance you can produce that?
[05:37] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely — we'll produce a sequence diagram showing ingress, routing (smart routing), model variant fallback, cache layers, and audit log delivery to your SIEM. Note: sometimes auto-transcribe calls it 'smart routing' as 'smart routing'...
[05:55] [00:06:00] Maya Chen: We should also call out configuration knobs relevant to marketplace buyers: batching windows, KV cache TTLs, quantization profiles, and autoscaling policies. Those affect unit cost and latency.
[06:20] Sofia Morales: On quantization — do you have recommended profiles for AuroraCloud's GPU types? we run a mix of A100 and 80GB+ cards.
[06:35] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we maintain a model performance catalog; recommended quant profiles depend on model family and sequence length. For 80GB we typically run higher precision; we can add a small table to the ref arch doc with expected throughput/latency numbers.
[06:55] Rajat Singh: Bench question — our SLA asks for p95 < 120ms for small chat messages, is that achievable on dedicated or private?
[07:10] Diego Alvarez: p95 very workload dependent. For short context chat we see p95 sub-100ms on Dedicated with optimized kernels and warm KV cache; on Private with similar hardware we can reach same, but depends on network egress and sequence length — we'll include benchmark configs.
[07:40] Lena Park: ok please include the exact test harness and sample prompts for the certification run.
[07:50] Diego Alvarez: We'll share the benchmark script, which uses continuous batching patterns and records per-token breakdowns, plus example payloads.
[08:00] [00:08:15] Sofia Morales: Marketplace also asks for upgrade/rollback testing steps — how do you handle canaries/rollouts?
[08:18] Maya Chen: Redwood supports canary deploys, A/B rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. For private deployments we provide helm-based rollouts and a simple toggle to fall back to a pinned model variant if a new model fails QA. We'll document the steps.
[08:40] Rajat Singh: For networking we need to confirm IP ranges and whether outbound NAT is required. Also curious if you support private link or direct connect equivalents?
[08:55] Diego Alvarez: We support standard VPC peering and private link-style connections depending on cloud; for on-prem we support direct connection. We'll include required IP ranges and ports in the manifest doc.
[09:15] Lena Park: Any restrictions on logging? we require that PII is redacted prior to being stored in central logs.
[09:28] Maya Chen: Redwood's audit logs can be configured to redact or mask sensitive fields; for Private you control log storage so you can apply additional processors. We'll note masking best practices in the runbook.
[09:45] [00:10:00] Diego Alvarez: Quick note about model artifacts and signing: if you want higher assurance, we can sign bundles and include attestation metadata. That fits market place requirements for tamper-evidence.
[10:05] Sofia Morales: Great. Regarding the marketplace listing checklist — do you have an example filled checklist?
[10:12] Maya Chen: We do; we'll attach a sample checklist showing required docs, diagrams, and the security questionnaire answers we usually provide.
[10:25] Rajat Singh: On billing and metering — does Redwood expose per-route token breakdowns we can show to our customers via the marketplace billing UI?
[10:37] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns per route and model; for marketplace listings we can export a sample report.
[10:50] Lena Park: Good. Another item: customer-managed KMS - what key rotation cadence do you support and how is rotation handled without downtime?
[11:05] Diego Alvarez: Rotation is supported with a double-write window; keys are staged and then rolled, the runtime supports key versions. We'll include a short paragraph in the ref arch on rotation best practices.
[11:25] [00:11:40] Sofia Morales: Are there any known blockers for AuroraCloud if we go with the recommended Private deploy? like specific kernel versions or distro requirements?
[11:40] Diego Alvarez: We support mainstream k8s versions (1.25+ recommended), and need access to some kernel features for the inference runtime (hugepages, nvidia drivers with recommended versions). We'll include exact pre-reqs in the manifest.
[12:00] Maya Chen: We'll capture a pre-checklist that AuroraCloud infra can run before we start install.
[12:10] Rajat Singh: On the topic of observability, what tracing hooks do you provide? we want to link Redwood traces into our distributed tracing.
[12:25] Diego Alvarez: We provide tracing hooks and can forward spans to Jaeger/OTLP endpoints; token-level tracing and per-model traces are available — will document config endpoints.
[12:45] [00:13:10] Lena Park: For the marketplace listing, we sometimes have compliance scans that look for open ports or risky defaults — will your helm chart lock down ingress by default?
[12:58] Diego Alvarez: Chart defaults are secure by default: ingress disabled, service only ClusterIP, and we provide optional ingress templates with examples for load balancer or private link.
[13:15] Sofia Morales: On lifecycle: how do you manage model version pins vs auto-updates? customers may want to pin a model for stability.
[13:28] Maya Chen: You can pin model versions per-route; we also offer rollout policies to promote new model versions once validated. For marketplace we recommend a documented default pinned version and a tested upgrade path.
[13:45] Rajat Singh: Can we get a short example manifest for a pinned route?
[13:52] Diego Alvarez: yes will include sample route config in values.yaml.
[14:00] [00:14:30] Lena Park: About the bench — we'd like to run tests that simulate 2k RPS for embeddings workloads and chat workloads at 200 RPS. can you support that from your side?
[14:20] Diego Alvarez: We can support those scales on Dedicated or Private with right hardware; for test we will propose a config and expected hardware (list of instance types), and if you're okay we can run the bench during your maintenance window.
[14:40] Sofia Morales: please include expected costs for the suggested hardware in the doc, even rough estimates.
[14:50] Maya Chen: We'll include example cost profiles and how batching/cache reduce per-token cost.
[15:00] [00:15:30] Rajat Singh: Any special notes on GPU drivers? we like to avoid vendor-specific pins but need stability.
[15:10] Diego Alvarez: We'll add recommended driver versions and a short troubleshooting note.
[15:22] Lena Park: For the marketplace submission we also need a joint solution blurb and partner logo usage rights, who owns that?
[15:35] Maya Chen: Redwood marketing will provide a standard joint solution blurb and logo assets; I'll loop in marketing after this call.
[15:45] [00:16:30] Sofia Morales: circling back to audit — we need to ensure we can demonstrate end-to-end log retention policies. Can you support configurable retention windows?
[15:58] Diego Alvarez: Yes, retention is configurable, and for Private you control the retention. We'll show examples for 30/90/365 day configs.
[16:15] Rajat Singh: Ok let's talk about deliverables and owners.
[16:25] Maya Chen: Owners: Maya will draft the reference arch + joint solution blurb; Diego will share helm chart, manifest, and bench scripts; AuroraCloud (Rajat) will share compliance checklist and available windows for the POC.
[16:41] [00:17:10] Lena Park: Sounds good. One small question: for marketplace listing, do you support a 'bring your own model' story? some of our buyers want to deploy their model artifact.
[16:55] Diego Alvarez: Yes, BYOM is supported—our runtime can load customer artifacts with proper attestation and registry config. We'll document the artifact layout.
[17:10] Sofia Morales: Great. Also, for the reference arch diagram can you show both cloud and hybrid flows?
[17:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll provide separate diagrams: hosted marketplace flow, private VPC flow, and hybrid with on-prem.
[17:30] [00:18:00] Rajat Singh: Any questions from Redwood on AuroraCloud constraints?
[17:40] Lena Park: We'll share a short doc with expected certification timeline and any compliance restrictions (data residency, allowed clouds, etc.).
[17:52] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll also propose two benchmark windows next week; please confirm availability.
[18:05] Diego Alvarez: I'll add a note - bench requires svc account and temporary ingress rules; we will provide step-by-step.
[18:20] [00:18:50] Sofia Morales: ok one admin ask: where should we upload the artifacts? we have a partner repo on auroracloud partners.
[18:30] Maya Chen: Either link to your partner repo or we can push to a shared S3; let's decide over email.
[18:40] Rajat Singh: fine. Anything else?
[18:48] Maya Chen: Quick recap of next steps and action items...
[18:55] [00:19:20] -- Recap --
[19:00] Maya Chen: Action items: Maya to send reference arch draft + runbook, Diego to share helm + bench scripts, Rajat to provide compliance checklist and schedule for POC. We'll aim to have docs by 2026-03-10 and bench window week of 2026-03-16.
[19:25] Lena Park: thanks, we'll review and respond.
[19:35] Sofia Morales: thanks all, bye.
[19:40] Diego Alvarez: thanks, bye.
[19:45] [00:20:00] -- End of recording --

Notes about transcription: some speaker labels may be generic; occasional transcription errors on acronyms (KMS sometimes transcribed as K-M-S).
